MINUTES
  MALIBU PLANNING COMMISSION
  REGULAR MEETING
  AUGUST 1, 2022
  TELECONFERENCED VARIOUS LOCATIONS
  -

  6:30 P.M.

The following meeting was held pursuant to the Governor’s Executive Orders N-25-20
and N-29-20 and fully teleconferenced from various locations during the coronavirus
disease (COVID-19) pandemic.

CALL TO ORDER

  Chair Hill called the meeting to order at 6:30 p.m.

ROLL CALL

  The following persons were recorded in attendance by the Recording Secretary:

  PRESENT: Chair Kraig Hill, Vice Chair Dennis Robert Smith, and Commissioners Jeffrey
  Jennings, John Mazza, and Mark Wetton

  ALSO PRESENT: Richard Mollica, Planning Director; Adrian Fernandez, Assistant
  Planning Director; Patrick Donegan, City Attorney; Trevor Rusin, Assistant City Attorney;
  Jesse Bobbett, Community Services Director; Raneika Brooks, Senior Planner; Jessica
  Thompson, Senior Planner; Coli Turner, Planning Technician and Rebecca Evans,
  Recording Secretary

APPROVAL OF AGENDA

MOTION  Commissioner Mazza moved and Commissioner Jennings seconded a motion to
  approve the agenda as recommended by staff, with Item No. 5 .B. continued to a
  date uncertain.

  The question was called and the motion carried unanimously.

REPORT ON POSTING OF AGENDA

  Recording Secretary Evans reported that the agenda for the meeting was properly
  posted on July 22, 2022.

ITEM 1  CEREMONIAL/PRESENTATIONS
  None.
   Malibu Planning Commission
  Minutes of August 1, 2022
  Page 2 of 9

ITEM 2.A.  PUBLIC COMMENTS

  J.R. Rucker stated he had purchased tickets for himself and his colleagues to attend
  the Jazz Festival. He felt the festival had unsafe walking conditions, and was
  considering pursuing legal actions against the individual who co-sponsored the
  festival. He urged the Commission not to co-sponsor future events with individuals
  they didn’t have faith in.

ITEM 2.B.  COMMISSION I STAFF COMMENTS

  Commissioner Mazza stated the Planning Commission held a meeting on the
  JazzFest last Thursday, and that J.R. Rucker could find the information he needed
  in the agenda report for the Special meeting. Commissioner Mazza clarified that
  the event was not sponsored in any way by the City.

  Vice Chair Smith acknowledged that the Planning Director’s decision to revoke the
  Temporary Use Permit was likely correct in hindsight.

  Commissioner Wetton stated that he had driven by the area mid-day and it appeared
  organizers were not close to being ready to go and he had heard from an attendee
  that the event seemed extremely disorganized.

  Chair Hill stated that on Friday night he had received phone calls saying that
  alcohol was still advertised and had emailed City Manager Steve McClary and
  Planning Director Richard Mollica to ask if the event would be cancelled due to
  lack of compliance with the Planning Commission condition. Chair Hill wondered
  if the written minutes could be more of a guide to the video. Chair Hill reminded
  that the California Coastal Commission (CCC) review of the Short-Term Rental
  (STR) Ordinance was scheduled for Friday, August 12th~ He stated that CCC’s
  concern appeared to be that Malibu was daytime visitor serving and asked if there
  were any reports to support that most of the visitors we serve were not overnight
  visitors.

  Commissioner Wetton stated that Malibu was in a unique situation and it was a
  question of having a lot of expensive property here, and most of the Accessory
  Dwelling Units (ADUs) may become guest houses with more latitude on the
  building codes rather than adding to the supply of low-cost housing.

  Chair Hill stated that residents were being forced out of Malibu neighborhoods with
  a range of things like STRs, ADUs and Real Estate Investment Trusts. He asked if
  the City maintained numbers related to this topic.
   Malibu Planning Commission
  Minutes of August 1, 2022
  Page 3 of 9

 Vice Chair Mazza noted that the hearing will focus on STRs and that the California
 Coastal Commission has indicated that they will not accept the City’s decision.

Planning Director Mollica stated that the next meeting would start at 5:30 p.m. as
a special meeting and conclude by 6:30 p.m. in order to start the regular meeting.
The Election of Chair and Vice Chair would occur in September. The California
Coastal Commission would meet in Calabasas on Friday and they were
recommending denial of the changes the City wanted, in particular the hosted STR
changes.

In response to Chair Hill, Planning Director Mollica agreed there was a high
volume of daytime visitors to the area and the Los Angeles County Department of
Beaches and Harbors had data on how many visitors used Malibu beaches. He
stated that the CCC objected to the loss of campground sites next to Bluffs Park.
He agreed that ADUs may create some issues from those who want to capitalize on
deed restricted ADUs.

Planning Director Mollica noted the City had received a number of phone calls and
emails on the Sunset Jazz Fest and the City had prepared a press release on the
topic, which included the City’s role as a lessor for the event site rather than an
event partner. There was an issue with a lack of communications regarding parking.
The information was shared with the City Manager and the Planning Department
had begun working with the Public Works Department on improved
communication during project review.

In response to Chair Hill, Planning Director Mollica stated that staff conducted two
scans of the public website and found references to an onsite bar. The applicant was
contacted and they stated that the bar would only serve water, Gatorade, and other
non-alcoholic beverages. City staff were onsite to document that no alcohol service
or sales took place. He stated that both he and the Community Services Director
responded to questions and issues on the day of the event. The code enforcement
hotline was available to leave messages over the weekend and the Sheriffs
Department was available for immediate issues. Code Enforcement was currently
short-staffed and positions were open for applications.

Chair Hill asked ifthe code enforcement hotline was prominent on the City website.

Commissioner Mazza suggested hiring retired sheriffs who may want to double dip
on their pensions for code enforcement. He shared that the CCC would hold a
seminar on sea level rise at the same time as the Planning Commission meeting and
asked if those meetings were overlapping.
   Malibu Planning Commission
  Minutes of August 1, 2022
  Page 4 of 9

  Planning Director Mollica stated that Senior Planners and a coastal engineer would
  attend the session on sea level rise. The session would be available online after the
  meeting.

  Chair Hill noted a false advertising connotation to the term open bar without a
  qualifier that stated it was non-alcoholic.

ITEM 3  CONSENT CALENDAR

  The Consent Calendar consisted of the following items:

  A.  Previously Discussed Items
  None.

  B.  New Items

  1.  Approval of Minutes
  Recommended Action: Approve the minutes of the September 8, 2021
  Regular Planning Commission meeting.
  Staff Contact: Administrative Assistant Evans, 456-2489, ext. 246

MOTION  Commissioner Mazza moved and Commissioner Jennings seconded a
  motion to approve the minutes of the September 8, 2021 Regular Planning

  The question was called and the motion carried 4-1, Commissioner Wetton

  yards, for a home destroyed in the 2018 Woolsey Fire, located in the Rural
  Residential- Five Acre zoning district at 31113 Bailard Road (Ellis)

FRIENDLY AMENDMENT
  Commissioner Jennings proposed a Friendly Amendment to add a condition of
  approval stating, “Prior to the issuance of any development permit, the
  applicant/property owner shall provide a pre-construction assessment of the
  existing condition of Bailard Road to the subject parcel. A copy of this assessment
  shall be kept on file with the City: The applicant/property owner shall be
   Malibu Planning Commission
  Minutes of August 1, 2022
  Page 6 of 9

  responsible for repairs of any damage to the road that may result during the
  construction phase of the proposed project. Any obvious damage to the road that
  becomes apparent during the construction phase (including, but not limited to,
  potholes, cracks and ripples) shall be immediately repaired by the
  applicants/property owner. Prior to a Planning Department final inspection, the
  applicant/property owner shall submit a post-construction assessment of the road
  to demonstrate compliance with this condition. A photo survey shall be utilized to
  complete this assessment. Alternatively, the property owner/applicant may reach
  an agreement with the entity that maintains the road for an in lieu payment to repair
  this segment of the private road.”

  The friendly amendment was accepted by the seconder of the motion.

  The Commission discussed the motion and directed questions to staff.

  The question was called and the motion carried 3-2, Commissioner Mazza and
  Chair Hill dissenting.

MOTION  At 8:54 p.m. Chair Hill recessed the meeting. The meeting reconvened at 9:00 p.m.
  with all Commissioners present.
